title: Ashaveri Inference Receipt (JSON twin of the CBOR/COSE wire format)
description: Display-only projection of the signed COSE_Sign1 receipt. The CBOR bytes are canonical; this JSON form is never signed directly. The payload branch describes both versions the CDDL defines: receipt-v1's thirteen fields, and receipt-v2, which is those same fields plus the marking attestation. Each branch is closed, so a member its version does not name is a refusal here exactly as it is in the CDDL and in the parser. Closure is not one level: the payload map and the four nested inside it, `meas`, `att`, `tok` and `mk`, are closed, so a member one of them does not name is refused at that level too rather than read here and dropped on the way to a verifier. The payload branches refuse an unnamed member through `unevaluatedProperties`, which is the keyword that reaches through their `allOf`, and the nested definitions through `additionalProperties`, which is the one that applies where the members are named in the same object. `protectedHeader` carries the three labels the CDDL declares and no more, and this definition carries no closure keyword: the parser reads that map by number and accepts only those three labels, so a document carrying another is refused before any projection of it is built and an unnamed label never arrives here as a field left out, and the parser decodes that map where no floating-point number can appear, because a label written as the float 1.0 takes the map slot of the integer 1 and is no longer distinguishable from it afterwards. The unprotected map is the format's one declared carrier of no claim, outside the signature and outside this projection.

kid.description: sha256 of the Ed25519 public key, hex

payload.description: Exactly one branch per payload version. `v` is which one the document is, and the branches are exclusive on it.

signature.description: Ed25519 signature over the Sig_structure, hex

m.description: SHA-256 for a software deployment, the platform's SHA-384 measurement for a TEE

payloadV1.description: A v1 document and nothing else. The map is closed: `unevaluatedProperties` refuses any member payloadFields and `v` do not name, so a v1 payload cannot carry a marking attestation, and a reader never has to work out what became of a member it did not read.

sch.description: a label from the marking-scheme registry. Not an enum here because the CDDL admits any tstr: the registry this package reads is `none` and `provenance-v1`, and it refuses a label outside those two as UNSUPPORTED_SCHEME rather than this twin deciding the format.

d.description: sha256 of the marked region exactly as it appears in the response, not of the whole response. For `sch: "none"` the region is empty and this is the digest of no bytes.

payloadV2.description: A v2 document and nothing else. The map is closed the same way v1's is: fourteen members are the whole of it, so a member outside this list is a malformed payload rather than a member a reader agreed to forget.
